title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Turns 100 — a Little Late, but Bigger Than Ever
summary:
New York's most famous parade is turning 100 — and this year, it is running a little late. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was first scheduled for Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, but strong winds and the chance of flooding pushed it to Saturday, November 28. It is the first time the parade has ever been postponed. Safety worries about the giant balloons also played a part in the decision. The good news? The show is still going on, and it is bigger than ever.

The parade airs live at 8:30 a.m. ET on NBC and Telemundo, and it streams on Peacock. Parade officials say 95% of the acts planned for Thursday will still perform on Saturday. Two marching bands — the Macy's Great American Marching Band and the University of Alabama's Million Dollar Band — cannot make it because of scheduling conflicts. But there are surprise additions: LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor will join the lineup.

This year features a record-breaking 100 inflatables, including new balloons of Bluey, Hello Kitty, Mickey Mouse and Underdog. RAYE opens the music, followed by performances from Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Queen Latifah, JoJo, RIIZE, EJAE, Keke Palmer, Anthony Ramos and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots. Megan Hilty will perform a special tribute to Dolly Parton, and there will also be a Broadway showcase. Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker return to host NBC's coverage.

Want to watch for free? Peacock does not offer a free trial, but some streaming services that carry NBC, Telemundo or Peacock do. Viewers can get seven days of Peacock Premium Plus free as an add-on through Amazon Prime Video. Free trials are also available through DirecTV, Fubo and Hulu + Live TV. Just keep an eye out for weather-related updates before tuning in.
why_it_matters: The first postponement in the parade's history shows how even a long-running tradition must change its plans when safety is at risk. It also affects everyone who planned to watch on Thursday, since they must now tune in on Saturday instead.

background_read: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is a huge parade in New York City that takes place on Thanksgiving Day, with giant character balloons, marching bands and live music.
It is put on by the Macy's department store and has become a holiday tradition that many families watch on television or from the streets.
The giant balloons are the stars of the show, but they are hard to control when the wind is strong, so safety comes first.
That is why bad weather can force the parade to change its plans, even in the year it turns 100.
